head: c6531982c43af1445979ce014493c7cfe8b2c214
method: own script dot-sources scripts/gpu-window-guard.ps1, calls Start-GuardSampler -CsvPath <scratch>/samples.csv -IntervalMs 250, waits 400 ms + 1.0 s + 2.2 s (>= 3 s), then Stop-GuardSampler -TimeoutSeconds 10; CSV parsed independently with Import-Csv; run under both pwsh 7.6.7 and Windows PowerShell 5.1
checks_summary: samples.csv exists with the documented header; rows == returned samples; >= 10 samples in >= 3 s; seq is 1..n; timestamps monotonic and parseable; numeric fields parse; used peak / free min / util max re-computed from the CSV equal Stop-GuardSampler's stats; the child exits; stop file removed; no sampler-loop process remains (Get-CimInstance command-line scan); CSV can be opened exclusively afterwards (no leaked file handle)
no_start_job: the fixed template contains no Start-Job call (only a comment explaining why Start-Job was replaced); the sampler runs scripts/gpu-guard-sampler-loop.ps1 as a real child process
gpu_work: only read-only nvidia-smi --query-gpu queries from the loop; no CUDA API reference (cudarc/CudaContext/nvrtc) exists in the changed scripts
conclusion: sampler persistence works in both shells: every 0.25 s sample is flushed immediately, Stop joins the child and returns stats that match an independent CSV recompute, and nothing is left running or locked.
